text:
anya: Quick heads-up from bring-up of 'astra-lite-6b' (converted from gemma-format) — after an int4 pass the model looks ok on short prompts but starts repeating around ~1k tokens. suspect rotary frequency scaling + tokenizer normalization interaction. sharing early diffs.

devon: paste the failing prompt and short/long metrics? which convert tool/version?

anya: convert: tools/convert-gemma-to-redwood v0.9.3. sample prompt and metrics:
```
Prompt: "Write a long technical analysis of progressive quantization strategies..."
Short (<=128): ppl 12.4
Long (~2048): ppl 48.1, repetition spikes after 1024
```

liam: that pattern smells like a rotary mismatch across head groups — if headwise scaling was applied differently during conversion we see prefix coherence collapse. did the convert script apply headwise rescale?

anya: yes, conversion included a "shim_layer" that applied a linear per-head scale to approximate gemma->qwen rotaries. snippet:
```
# conv shim
for h in range(n_heads):
    scale[h] = base_scale * (1 - 0.02 * (h / n_heads))
```
We thought it was harmless.

maya: also check tokenizer normalizer — our converted tokenizer strips soft hyphens (U+00AD) and collapses some combining diacritics. token index shifts in long docs could misalign kv-cache and amplify rotary issues. run tokenizer.debug on the long prompt.

devon: agree. anya, can you diff original gemma tokenizer vs converted tokenizer on the same plaintext? token mismatches are a red flag.

anya: did that — about 0.8% token index shifts on long text from soft-hyphen + ZWJ handling. sample diff snippet:
```
orig: [ ... 1021:'word', 1022:'\u00AD', 1023:'suffix' ]
conv: [ ... 1021:'word\u00AD', 1022:'suffix' ]
```

liam: token shifts plus per-head rotary shim is a plausible two-factor failure. token shifts change positional mapping to kv-cache; if rotary freq is headwise-warped attention patterns degrade.

onboard-bot: Dedicated repro spun up: ded-ast-03 (GPU: a100-80g). link: http://infra/internal/ded-ast-03. logs + eval harness queued.

maya: running tokenization-only regression across several long docs and dumping token offsets.

devon: while that's running try an ablation: 1) disable shim_layer (uniform scale=1.0) 2) keep converted tokenizer 3) run longctx eval. if behavior improves shim is likely primary.

anya: started ablation job on ded-ast-03 id 17856011. ETA ~8m.

liam: also try reapplying NFKC normalization that gemma used before conversion to see if token index shifts go away.

ops: allocated extra artifact storage for the evals, ETA 2m.

anya: update: ablation with shim disabled dropped longctx ppl 48.1 -> 18.7 and repetition disappeared in the sample. shim appears to be main culprit.

maya: so the heuristic headwise warp introduced harmful frequency distortion. we should revert shim and compute deterministic freq mapping from model dims instead of linear headwise fudge.

liam: agreed. plan: revert shim, compute freq_table using canonical formula (e.g., freq = base * head_multiplier**head_index) and fit to original checkpoint params via small L2 fit. no ad-hoc per-head slope.

devon: open PR to add tokenizer parity tests in onboarding harness: token index parity for 2k-window documents. conversion should warn/fail if parity deviates beyond threshold.

anya: filing issue/PR: #onboard/ast-headwarp-fix. will push revert + recalculated freq_table, then re-run int4 quant with per-channel scaling ON and OFF.

onboard-bot: job 17856011 completed. logs -> https://artifacts.internal/17856011. summary: shim off yields baseline-like longctx behavior.

maya: follow-ups: (1) bisect when shim landed, (2) update convert tool to deterministic freq estimator + opt-in headwise scaling, (3) add token parity gate, (4) run 24h eval on dedicated infra to catch slow regressions.

ops: scheduled 24h run on ded-ast-03, starts in 10m.

liam: note for docs: call out soft-hyphen and ZWJ differences between tokenizers and provide a normalization toggle. mark headwise scaling as experimental and opt-in.

anya: thanks everyone — pushing PRs now and will report back with final numbers. :thumbsup:
